title: Split Compass: Interactive runbook for asymmetric traffic splits and emergency rollback
creator: Priya Singh
description: Design and prototype an interactive runbook ("Split Compass") embedded in the Redwood Console that helps engineers and PMs compose, preview, and safely execute asymmetric traffic splits across variants. The runbook should support a) guided canary and A/B flows with cohort targeting, b) a simulation canvas to preview request-level and aggregate effects (latency p50/p95 overlay, error rate delta, cost delta), c) explicit rollback paths with one-click emergency snapback and staged revert playbooks, and d) explainable guardrails that tie to existing policy thresholds (SLO, cost budget, security gates). Goal: reduce cognitive load when performing non-50/50 splits and make emergency rollback consistent and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive canvas allows creating asymmetric splits (e.g., 10% variant A, 3% variant B, remainder baseline) and persists policy constraints
Simulation mode shows projected latency, error rate, and cost deltas for the chosen split and time window
Emergency rollback action is reachable in ≤2 clicks from the runbook and records an audit entry with user, timestamp, and reason
UI surfaces a confidence indicator that maps to rollout automation (auto-advance, manual step, blocked by guardrail)
Figma prototype passes stakeholder review and usability test with 5 engineering / 3 PM participants
tasks: Finalize information architecture for split composer and simulation sidebar

ui_notes: Use tokenized chips for cohort definitions (region, header, user_segment) with inline validation
Drag handle snapping: 1% increments by default, shift+drag for 0.1% precision
Accessibility: keyboard-first composer, ARIA live region for simulation updates
Animations: subtle easing for weight transitions (150ms) to make changes discoverable

Run 5 flows: even split, 10/90 asymmetric, multi-variant 3-way, rolling ramp, emergency rollback test
Collect qualitative feedback from testers and quantitative telemetry comparing predicted vs actual deltas
